newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram says to review forex rules.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram says to review forex rules.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday that the country's foreign exchange rules would be reviewed and corporate managements made more accountable, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

"The FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) review will take note of the liberalisation and changes in the foreign exchange regime and need for further liberalisation in the context of demand for full convertibility (of the rupee)...," Chidambaram was quoted as saying in an interview.
He said the review of FERA was part of a law against money laundering to be introduced in parliament in its budget session in February.
"I do not rule in or rule out anything," Chidambaram said in response to a question on full rupee convertibility.
Chidambaram said the Companies Act would be amended to put in place a more deregulative and decentralised system, coupled with tighter enforcement.

"Today it is micro-management. Companies must have freedom but within the regulated freedom there should be greater corporate democracy, greater reliance on full disclosures, greater accountability of managements to shareholders," he said.
